new.text: Explanation of ara::com API AUTOSAR AP R25-11 5.3.6.1 One-Way aka Fire-and-Forget Methods Before proceeding with the functionalities provided for “normal” methods, we briefly introduce “one-way methods” here as we already referred to this term in the previous section. ara::com supports a special flavor of a method, which we call “one-way” or “fire-and-forget”. Technically this is a method with only IN-params — no OUT-params and no raising of errors allowed. There is also no hand-shaking/synchronisation pos- sible with the server! The client/caller therefore gets no feedback at all, whether the server/callee has processed a “one-way” call or not (except for a possible recoverable Error ( ComErrc::kNetworkBindingFailure ) in the returned ara::core::Re- sult object). There are communication patterns, where such a best-effort approach is fully suffi- cient. In this case such a “one-way/fire-and-forget” semantics is very light-weight from a resource perspective. If we look at the signature of such a method, we see, that it is simpler, than that from a regular method:

used.text: Specification of Communication Management AUTOSAR AP R25-11 [SWS_CM_00197] Asynchronous behavior of method call with notification Upstream requirements: RS_CM_00213, RS_CM_00215, RS_AP_00114, RS_AP_00127, RS_- AP_00138 ⌈ To achieve asynchronous behavior of the method call with event-driven notification on the result availability, the non-blocking method then() of ara::core::Future object shall be used. It allows to register a function, which gets asynchronously called in case the future has a valid result. ⌋ Note: In order to report an ApApplicationError (according to the interface descrip- tion in the Manifest), the implementation of a service method stores the corresponding ara::core::ErrorCode representing this ApApplicationError (see [16]) into the ara::core::Promise object, from which the ara::core::Future is returned to the caller of the service method implementation. This ara::core::ErrorCode will then be used by the respective network binding to include the error information in the method response message (see e.g., [SWS_CM_10308] and [SWS_CM_10428] for the SOME/IP network binding or [SWS_CM_11102] and [SWS_CM_10431] for the DDS network binding). [SWS_CM_00822] Minimum Send Interval monitoring for for method calls by the client ⌈ To protect receivers from flooding/overload, each method shall have a config- urable Minimum Send Interval (see ServiceInterfaceDeploymentElement . min- imumSendInterval ), which specifies the minimum amount of time that shall pass between two calls of the method by the client, i.e., the Minimum Send Interval limits the maximum Tx frequency of a given method call in the network. If the application calls a method by invoking the operator() of the respective method class, ara::com shall check, whether the time since the last successful handover of the method call the un- derlying transmission layer is greater than the specified Minimum Send Interval, i.e., the Minimum Send Interval is not violated. If the operator() has never been invoked before, this shall also successfully pass the Minimum Send Interval check. If the Mini- mum Send Interval is not violated, ara::com shall process the method call by handing it over to the transmission layer. The time of handover shall count as start of the new Minimum Send Interval monitoring. If the Minimum Send Interval is violated, ara::com shall discard the method call (see [SWS_CM_00196] and [SWS_CM_90435] ). If the method was a Request&Response method, the error code ComErrc::kMinimum- SendIntervalViolationError (see [SWS_CM_10432]) shall be returned via the ara::core::Future of the operator() . For Fire&Forget methods, the call shall be discarded, but no further error is reported back to the application, i.e., the applica- tion has to expect that F&F method calls are not executed in case of an Minimum Send Interval violation without further feedback by ara::com . The Minimum Send Interval shall only be check on the client side, i.e., by the instance that actually invokes the method call and not by the server/provider, which answers/accepts the method call. If the configured Minimum Send Interval ( ServiceInterfaceDeploymentElement . minimumSendInterval ) of a method has the value 0, the Minimum Send Interval monitoring shall not be active for the corresponding operator() . ⌋ 301 of 675 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement
